title: Police station torched in Hasina's home town Tungipara; BNP farm-wing leader killed in Faridpur
dek: Crowds freed detainees from Tungipara police station and burned a BNP MP's house on Tuesday night, a day after Bangladesh sent border troops into Gopalganj. Buses were set alight in Dhaka.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A crowd stormed and set fire to the police station in Tungipara, the ancestral home of former Bangladeshi prime minister Sheikh Hasina, on Tuesday night after police arrested several local activists of her banned Awami League, and the house of a lawmaker from the ruling BNP was burned soon after, according to reports and local officials. In neighbouring Faridpur district, a local leader of the BNP's farmers' wing died after a crude bomb exploded during a pro-Awami League procession.

The violence came a day after Bangladesh deployed Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) troops and armoured vehicles in Gopalganj district, and two days before a "lockdown" the Awami League has called for Thursday, 19 November.

## What happened

Witnesses said a crowd gathered outside Tungipara police station after announcements from mosque loudspeakers, according to reports. Police fired sound grenades, tear gas and rubber bullets, then withdrew from the station, and protesters entered the compound and set structures on fire. Residents said supporters of the banned Chhatra League, the Awami League's student wing, took away the people held in the station's lock-up; nearly 30 suspected activists had been detained there, one report said.

Between about 8.30 pm and 9 pm local time (8 pm to 8.30 pm IST), fire broke out at the Patgati Bazar home of BNP MP SM Jilani, Tungipara's chief administrator, Upazila Nirbahi Officer Mohammad Didarul Alam, confirmed. "Apparently, following the arrest of several people, they attacked the police station," he said, according to reports. Around 9 pm, four vehicles, two of them belonging to the BGB, were set on fire on the Gopalganj-Tungipara road, and road blockades stopped a fire engine from reaching the police station.

In Bhanga, in Faridpur district, Raju Molla, 34, joint organising secretary of the local unit of the Krishak Dal, the BNP's farmers' wing, was declared dead on arrival at the upazila health complex after a crude bomb exploded near him during a pro-Awami League procession that set out at about 9.15 pm. The local BNP president, Khandaker Iqbal Hossain Selim, blamed Awami League activists; Additional Superintendent of Police Md Raihan Gafur said police could not immediately confirm the cause of death, according to reports.

In Dhaka, at least four parked buses were set on fire between 8.45 pm and 11.15 pm and crude bombs were set off in several places, with no casualties reported, according to reports.

## What each side says

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told parliament that those who attacked the police station and law enforcement personnel would be identified through video and audio recordings and photographs "and be brought under the law". He said about 200 police were stationed at Tungipara but the government had held back "to avoid further casualties", and alleged that former Awami League ministers and MPs living abroad had encouraged the arson, according to reports.

The Leader of the Opposition, Jamaat-e-Islami chief Shafiqur Rahman, asked in parliament what the government had done beyond reshuffling officials. Authorities had earlier withdrawn Gopalganj's deputy commissioner, police superintendent and the officer in charge of Tungipara police station. A local leader of the banned party, speaking anonymously, blamed "unruly" activists for the fire but said the new officer in charge had provoked it with "unnecessary" arrests, according to reports.

## Why it matters for India

Ms Hasina has lived in India since August 2024, when an uprising drove her from power. A tribunal in Dhaka sentenced her to death in absentia a year ago, and the Awami League's political activities are banned. She said in an emailed interview this week that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December despite "the threat of death". Bangladesh's law minister, M Asaduzzaman, has said Dhaka has completed its legal process and the extradition decision rests with New Delhi, according to reports; India says the request is being examined under established legal procedures.

Gopalganj and Faridpur lie in south-western Bangladesh, the region closest to West Bengal, so prolonged unrest there is watched closely in Kolkata and along the border.

## What happens next

The Awami League's lockdown call for Thursday is the next test for the government in Dhaka, which has said it will act firmly if the unrest spreads.
